item.title: Who really owns the Albanian land Jared Kushner wants to turn into a 5-star resort?
item.description:
Who really owns the Albanian land Jared Kushner wants to turn into a 5-star resort?
November 24, 20269:24 AM ET
Rob Schmitz
The sun sets over coastal mountains near the city of Vlore, the region where Jared Kushner plans to build a five-star luxury resort. The land that Kushner bought for this project, though, is claimed by several local Albanians and its ownership is being investigated by state prosecutors.
Rob Schmitz/NPR
hide caption
toggle caption i
Rob Schmitz/NPR
ZVERNEC, Albania — In the summer of 2021, Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump boarded a yacht owned by Nat Rothschild, an heir to the European banking family. On the way from Montenegro to Greece, the yacht anchored off the coast of Albania.
And, as Kushner told an investment conference last year, that's when Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama arrived at the boat to tell them about his plan for the country.
"I was very impressed by what he wanted to do with the country," said Kushner. "I really didn't know anything about the country and I didn't understand the history, and the darkness of the history with the communism and terrible leadership led to it being fully undeveloped as a nation."

At least one family refuses the vitamin K injection for their newborn each day, on average, at Corewell Health's Butterworth Hospital in Grand Rapids, Michigan.
Kate Wells/KFF Health News

Every time Torrie LeBlanc failed to persuade a parent to give their baby a vitamin K injection, she thought about the blood-soaked diaper.
It belonged to a newborn delivered last year, in the bustling labor and delivery unit where LeBlanc worked as a physician at the Corewell Health hospital system in Grand Rapids, Mich.
This story was produced in partnership with KFF Health News.
In the early hours the day after the baby girl was born, she suddenly started bleeding "from everywhere," LeBlanc recalled. Her eyes, nose, and rectum all suddenly oozed blood.

item.title: Black travelers on Route 66 weren't welcome at most gas stations — except this one
item.description:
Black travelers on Route 66 weren't welcome at most gas stations — except this one
November 24, 20265:00 AM ET
By
Jennifer Vanasco
Edward Threatt stands outside the Threatt Filling Station in Luther, Okla., off Route 66. It was the only known Black-owned and operated gas station along the famous highway, according to the National Trust for Historic Preservation.
Nick Oxford for NPR
hide caption
toggle caption i
Nick Oxford for NPR
During the Jim Crow Era, Black families traveling Route 66, the historic highway that ran more than 2,000 miles from Chicago to Los Angeles, needed to carry food and gas with them. Most restaurants, gas stations and motels wouldn't serve them.
But there was one place they were guaranteed to find respite: a small, family-owned business just east of Oklahoma City that offered fuel, food and a place to stop for the night. The Threatt Filling Station, according to the National Trust for Historic Preservation, was the only known Black-owned and operated gas station along the famous Mother Road.

item.title: The human cost of the electric vehicle boom is at the center of a lawsuit in Congo
item.description:
Africa
The human cost of the electric vehicle boom is at the center of a lawsuit in Congo
Updated November 24, 20265:01 AM ET
Originally published November 24, 20265:00 AM ET
By
Emmet Livingstone
A neighborhood on the outskirts of Kolwezi, Democratic Republic of Congo, where industrial mines encroach on homes and open-pit operations increasingly consume residential areas, Sept. 27.
Marie Ruwet/AFP via Getty Images
hide caption
toggle caption i
Marie Ruwet/AFP via Getty Images
KOLWEZI, Democratic Republic of Congo — In a small cinderblock home in the scrub beside a Chinese-owned copper and cobalt mine in Kolwezi, a mother shares a story of devastating loss.
She believes pollution from the neighboring mine is responsible for her family's suffering.
She has lost three children. Two died at birth. A third suffered repeated nosebleeds before dying. One of her two surviving children has stunted growth.
Now she and 26 other residents are taking the company to court in a rare attempt to hold alleged polluters accountable in the Democratic Republic of Congo. They are also suing the government, accusing it of failing to enforce environmental regulations.

item.title: Democrats probe whether Trump Jr.-aligned businesses benefit from government access
item.description:
Politics
Democrats probe whether Trump Jr.-aligned businesses benefit from government access
November 24, 20265:00 AM ET
Eric McDaniel
Donald Trump Jr. speaks on stage on the second day of the 2026 Republican National Convention on Sept. 10, in Dallas.
Brandon Bell/Getty Images
hide caption
toggle caption i
Brandon Bell/Getty Images
Congressional Democrats, led by likely House Judiciary Committee Chair Rep. Jamie Raskin of Maryland, are expanding their investigation into the investment firm 1789 Capital, which brought on Donald Trump Jr. as a partner days after his father's reelection to the White House.
Since then, investigators say the firm has grown from "a middling venture capital firm" with $150 million in managed assets to "the darling of the venture capital world" with $3 billion in managed assets.
Investigators want to determine whether the growth was boosted by the president's son leveraging political influence or government information to secure federal contracts and regulatory changes for companies with connections to the investment firm.
